title.en: Job shop schedule and solver boundary

summary: Play back a schedule that a solver produced, and keep the boundary between solving and animating visible.
objective: Build a job shop floor where a computed schedule is played back on machines, with the makespan and the solver responsibility clearly stated.
intent_signals: Play back a machine schedule on a factory floor.
Show why a schedule cannot start a task before its predecessor finishes.
example_prompts: Build a job shop schedule playback with machines, tasks and a makespan readout.
Show a schedule violating a precedence constraint being rejected.
negative_signals: Not a solver implementation: unless a real solver runs, the schedule must be declared as supplied data.
Not a factory throughput or capacity study for any real plant.
not_for: Not a solver implementation: unless a real solver runs, the schedule must be declared as supplied data.
Not a factory throughput or capacity study for any real plant.

entities.name: Machines and tasks
entities.guidance: Model each machine as a station with a queue position and each task as an object carrying its job, duration and machine.

entities.name: Schedule timeline
entities.guidance: Show the schedule as a timeline in the scene with one lane per machine, so overlaps would be visible.

entities.name: Constraint report
entities.guidance: Validate the supplied schedule against precedence and no-overlap constraints and report violations by task.

state_contract.model: Jobs as ordered task sequences with nonnegative durations and machine assignments, and a supplied schedule of start times using half-open intervals so a task may start exactly when another ends. A validity check reports precedence and machine-overlap violations. A schedule that passes plays back in normal mode; a schedule that fails is either rejected or opened in a labelled diagnostic mode that shows the conflicting blocks as they were supplied. The makespan is the latest completion time. An empty schedule is a declared no-op.
state_contract.authority: The supplied schedule and the constraint checks are authoritative; the animation replays start times and may never move a task to make the picture look better.
actions: Play, pause and scrub the schedule.
Select a task and inspect its job, machine and constraints.
Load an invalid schedule and read the violation report.

invariants: In normal playback, which requires a schedule declared valid, no machine lane shows two tasks at once. In diagnostic mode overlaps are displayed exactly as supplied and clearly labelled as violations; the scene never silently reschedules or serialises them.
In normal playback a task never starts before its predecessor completes, with intervals half-open so that starting exactly at a predecessor completion is allowed rather than flagged.
The reported makespan equals the latest task completion time in the played schedule.
motion_guidance: Advance playback on a stated time scale with the simulated clock visible, so animation speed is never confused with duration.
Scrub backwards by restoring state from the schedule rather than by reversing an animation.
known_limits: Optimality is a property of the solver run, not of the playback; a played schedule is only optimal if the solver proved it.
Setup times, breakdowns, transport and operator availability are not modelled.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: In the job shop problem multiple jobs are processed on several machines, each job is a sequence of tasks that must be performed in order, no task may start before its predecessor completes, a machine can work on only one task at a time, a started task runs to completion, and the objective is to minimise the schedule length known as the makespan.
claims.scope: Problem definition and objective as documented. It constrains what a valid schedule is; it is not a claim that an arbitrary loaded schedule satisfies those constraints, which is why the scene validates input before normal playback.

source_refs.locator: The Job Shop Problem, problem statement and objective

object_craft.structure: Machine stations with an in-feed, a work area and an out-feed, and task carriers with printed job and duration labels.
object_craft.material: Neutral machine bodies with per-job carrier colours plus printed identifiers, so jobs remain distinguishable when colours repeat.
object_craft.articulation: Carriers move between stations at scheduled times. That travel is a display transition only: transport time is not part of the modelled schedule, and a carrier never occupies a machine outside its scheduled window.

object_craft.structure: A physical timeline rail with a lane per machine and blocks sized by duration.
object_craft.material: Opaque lane plates with gridlines at time units so durations can be read directly.
object_craft.articulation: A time cursor sweeps the rail in step with the floor animation.

physical_contract.scope: Time-indexed playback of a supplied schedule; no transport dynamics or contact.
checks: No machine has overlapping tasks at any playback time for a schedule declared valid; diagnostic mode is excluded from this check by construction.
Scrubbing to a time reproduces the same machine occupancy every time.
